Opening

LAUNCH · RE & World Views · Autumn 1 · Week 4

Festivals, shared values and the Day of Peace

Learning goal

Explain how a festival or shared value can bring people together and identify one value linked to peace.

How do beliefs and worldviews shape identity, values and choices?

I can explain an influence, compare two worldviews, identify a source of authority and give a structured explanation.

40 minutes, with flexible pauses. Point, speak, draw, type or write. A fictional example is welcome. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief.

Editable Word packPrintable pupil resources PDF

This is learning about religion and worldviews, not worship. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief, family detail or loss.

Word and evidence bank

A The Day of Peace

The United Nations International Day of Peace is held on 21 September each year. It invites everyone, of any worldview, to act for peace.

Authored summary of the United Nations observance

Limit: A day of peace does not end conflict. It asks people to act.

B A Christian example

Jesus taught “Blessed are the peacemakers”. Fictional case: a church runs a mediation group for neighbours in dispute.

Authored summary; Matthew 5:9

Limit: Belief and practice vary between individuals and communities.

C A Muslim example

The greeting “As-salamu alaykum” means “peace be upon you”. Fictional case: a mosque hosts an open day so neighbours can meet.

Authored RE summary

Limit: Belief and practice vary between individuals and communities.

D A Humanist example

Humanists argue that peace comes through reason, dialogue and human rights. Fictional case: a Humanist group runs a schools debate on resolving conflict.

Authored RE summary

Limit: Belief and practice vary between individuals and communities.

Independent

LAUNCH · RE & World Views · Autumn 1 · Week 4

Independent application

Choose one route and one response mode. Keep the same learning goal.

Supported task

  1. Choose one value from the word bank.
  2. Draw or label one action that shows it.
  3. Say how the action builds peace.

Use the glossary and one chunk of evidence. Plan the claim and supporting detail before explaining. Complete the organiser one space at a time. The value of ___ can lead to ___. This builds peace because ___.

An adult may read or scribe your exact response. They should not choose the answer.

Standard task

  1. Create a “Peace in Practice” response.
  2. Link one value to one real-life action.
  3. Explain how it brings people together.

The value of ___ can lead to ___. This builds peace because ___.

Check the required evidence and revise one detail.

Stretch task

  1. Link one value to actions from two worldviews.
  2. Explain the different reasons behind the same value.
  3. Judge which action would do most in your community, with a reason.

Choose the evidence independently. Use the frame only if it helps.

Explain why a shared value can unite people who disagree about belief.

Teacher brief

Teacher notes and answers

Teacher card

Festivals, shared values and the Day of Peace / LAUNCH_RE_A1_W04

Outcome: Explain how a festival or shared value can bring people together and identify one value linked to peace.

Evidence to retain: F: “Peace in Practice” response linking one value to one action.

Forty minute route

Arrival 4 min; starter 3; model 6; shared task 7; check 2; independent 12; review 3; exit 3. Pause time is flexible.

Preparation

Choose one independent route. Print the evidence and shared cards, required visual or data sheet, route worksheet and exit. The organiser is one separate A4 page. Keep answers with staff.

Use inclusive, non-devotional framing; keep personal belief optional; reinforce respectful comparison; support with concrete community examples.

Access and regulation

Visual examples; limited writing; values word bank; draw/label option; verbal explanation; quiet reflection alternative.

Offer a predictable start, private response and agreed pause. No cold calling or forced personal disclosure. Rejoin at one clearly named next step. Keep teen-appropriate examples and the same learning goal across response modes.

This is learning about religion and worldviews, not worship. Nobody is asked to share a personal belief, family detail or loss.

Assessment

Use questioning and the exit response to decide the next step. Record the learner’s individual contribution and the access support used.

UAS: no approved unit code is supplied. Match the learner’s evidence to the centre-selected unit and exact criteria before submission. This pack makes no automatic award claim.

Model and answers

Read these pages before teaching. Hide the model during independent assessment.

Question: Name one value shared across two worldviews.

Evidence: B A Christian example: Jesus taught “Blessed are the peacemakers”. Fictional case: a church runs a mediation group for neighbours in dispute. C A Muslim example: The greeting “As-salamu alaykum” means “peace be upon you”. Fictional case: a mosque hosts an open day so neighbours can meet.

Think aloud: For example, peace, welcome or dialogue.

Check: Is the Day of Peace only for religious people? No. It is for everyone.

Arrival answers

1. A source people trust to guide what they believe or do.

2. Something people of different worldviews agree is important

3. For example, peace, welcome or dialogue.

4. No. It is for everyone.

Shared activity reasoning

1. A mediation group for neighbours — Reconciliation. Card B: peacemaking in practice.

2. An open day so neighbours can meet — Welcome and understanding. Card C.

3. A debate on resolving conflict — Dialogue. Card D: reason and dialogue.

Exit responses

Name one value shared across two worldviews. For example, peace, welcome or dialogue.

Is the Day of Peace only for religious people? No. It is for everyone.

Teaching and evidence record

Supplied scheme of work teaching sequence: Arrival: 4 retrieval questions. Starter: choose which actions build peace in a community. I Do: introduce a festival/shared-value example and model symbol → meaning → value. We Do: compare short Christian, Muslim and Humanist examples of peace/community. You Do: create a small ‘Peace in Practice’ response linking one value to one real-life action. Exit ticket: one shared value across two worldviews.

Look for

F: “Peace in Practice” response linking one value to one action.

Accept accurate equivalents, including speech or exact scribing. Check the concept and use of evidence rather than length or handwriting. Record access support separately from content prompting.

BUILD: a concrete example with a reason or demonstrated action. GROW: explain or compare with a relevant detail. LAUNCH: connect evidence and reasoning; use a limitation when the outcome requires it. Keep RE responses non-GCSE.

Media

Original captioned teaching model made for this pack. It demonstrates the supplied reasoning; it is not historical footage, survivor testimony or a documentary. The full transcript and factual source credits are included.

Use manual steps for a calm pace. The silent MP4 has visible captions and a matching text transcript. External archive media is optional and should be previewed before class.
